---
title: "Candidate ensemble specification"
---

`cand_ensemble` follows `app/cards/template.py`: mutable and pipeline-compatible,
callable export, settled model/style options and enablement, background evaluation,
completed-evaluation signature export readiness, configuration restoration and code recording.

`ensemble.representatives` reads zero-based weighted winners from current
`tuning_results.review.representatives`. Read-only or missing evidence is rejected.
Each member is a complete unfitted evaluated pipeline. Models default to all
available methods; restored valid exclusions persist. The preferred metric is a
display setting and does not trigger fitting or affect representative selection.

`evaluate_ensemble` uses `pipeline_search.prepare` for the first selected member
to reuse plan validation, implicit resampling and weighting exclusions. Each
member is reused from a matching session artifact or cloned and fitted within each split. Member predictions and their
combination are scored on the same validation rows using task-specific scorers.
All supported metrics are collected once. Mean/median regression and aligned
probability/majority classification use equal member weights. Stacking is deferred.

`EnsembleEvaluation` retains the unfitted definition, per-split fitted ensembles,
split memberships and metric scores. These potentially large runtime objects are
shared across proxy clones, treated as read-only and regenerated when restored
ensemble export requires fitted models. The card's portable `evaluation` state
stores only aggregate metric tables, member labels, split count, origin and the
evaluation input signature. Matching saved scores restore both views without
fitting; they cannot satisfy the fitted export contract. Changed evaluation
inputs invalidate the saved display. Completed upstream evidence, including an
exhausted search, can trigger ensemble evaluation independently of new trials.
`proxy_data.ensemble_results` validates source data, roles, modelling context,
evaluation plan and active pipeline. `with_ensemble` rejects stale evaluations and
sets the active pipeline to one ensemble terminal step: complete member pipelines
must not be wrapped in duplicated upstream preprocessing. No full-data fit occurs.

Footer Apply/Ensemble controls downstream export. Disabled export is the unchanged
incoming proxy; enabled export waits for matching evaluation. No partially fitted
ensemble is exported. Background cancellation stops new submissions; a native fit already running
finishes in its worker, then releases any abandoned snapshot artifacts. Runtime fitting
errors must remain visible, not become successful empty results.

The front horizontal bars show selected members plus ensemble, best first by
signed scorer, losses displayed naturally. Orange distinguishes ensemble. Flip
side shows every feasible task metric mean, sorted by the preferred metric, with
preferred-metric fold SD and split count. Unavailable metrics are missing, not zero.
Repeated/grouped/temporal plans preserve the upstream memberships; post-selection
resampling is explicitly distinguished from independent test performance.

Tests cover five representatives, member subsets, median/mean combination,
training-only scalers, classification voting and weights, upstream plan reuse,
unfitted downstream definition, current runtime evidence, invalidation,
cancellation, sorted metrics, checkbox export and browser restoration.

Evaluation identity includes data, roles, modelling context, resampling plan,
seed, task, selected member trial IDs and complete pipelines, and ensemble style.
Progress publications, unrelated trials, changes to unselected winners and review
weights that leave the selected winners unchanged do not cancel or reject an
in-flight evaluation. Result and export readiness use the same identity; task
arguments retain the original matching snapshot until fitting inputs change.

At least two distinct available representatives must be selected. Invalid or single-member
requests cancel superseded work, clear stale diagnostics and show a waiting message
without invoking the evaluator. The second upstream member is selected by default
and starts evaluation automatically. Reducing the selection to one waits again.

Winner changes for the same selected methods/context are coalesced until the active
snapshot finishes. Collect publishes completed results independently of the active
task. Completed snapshots stay visible while newer winners evaluate, explicitly
labelled as older; export requires the latest exact evaluation signature. Data,
resampling, selected-member and style changes clear incompatible snapshots and
cancel old work. Cancelled tasks can restart after module resume. Cancellation
signals the scheduler to stop at its next queue boundary; running native fits
finish before releasing their leases.

Model controls rebuild only when method identities/task change, not on each new
winning trial ID: rebinding them would repeatedly reset Options' settling delay.

### Session fit reuse and native scheduling

`session_fit_service` is shared by training, candidate review and ensemble cards.
Fit identity includes the complete configured preprocessing/model pipeline and its
implementation, data/index/roles/target/task, seed, exact ordered split memberships,
core training implementation and installed dependency versions. It excludes the
scoring preference, search progress, review weights and ensemble aggregation style.
Training publishes fitted fold pipelines plus held-out responses to private session
joblib files; SQLite contains only coordination metadata. Candidate review pins the
current per-method winners and retires losing completed-trial artifacts. Without
a review consumer, completed-trial artifacts become evictable immediately. Portable
checkpoints, bookmarks and completed tuning evidence contain no cache references,
fitted objects or row-level responses.

The ensemble loads available winning fold models, fits only missing keys, and
scores cached responses using the existing sklearn scorers. Each required response
method is called once per fitted fold, independently of metric count. Mean, median
and voting combine held-out responses without additional fitting. Runtime ensembles
retain the actual split-fitted member pipelines for downstream use. A changed winner
invalidates only that member's folds; style/metric changes reuse existing fits.

Native search pools and the session ensemble executor use the same CPU/memory
leases. One CPU is reserved for the UI (minimum one fitting slot). Pending training
fits take precedence; while a training search is active, ensembles use at most
`max(1, floor(cpu_count / 5))` slots and only spare capacity. Existing fits finish
before yielding. Completed or fully paused searches release their reservation;
ensembles can then use remaining capacity. The shared memory allowance uses the
same stable quarter-of-system-RAM policy and per-fit estimates as training.
Search proposal generation and batch boundaries are unchanged.

A 2 GiB LRU allowance bounds evictable fitted artifacts. Current review winners and
current/evaluating snapshots are pinned separately and may exceed the allowance;
the footer reports that case. Models loaded by current snapshots are weakly indexed,
not retained again in a strong global model cache. Data contexts are temporary and
released after their jobs finish. Unserializable fitted providers fall back to local
fitting under the same leases and may reuse live models; the footer reports the
fallback. Cancellation releases abandoned pins after late jobs finish. Session
shutdown closes workers and removes the private directory; dead-session directories
are swept on the next native session. Shinylive uses sequential, in-memory reuse of
selected members and opens no SQLite database or process executor.


Enabled export uses the evaluated source snapshot and depends on fitting identity,
not every incoming progress publication, so an already-ready export remains ready.
Footer enablement validates the collected evaluation's fitting signature against
current selected winners, rather than comparing the task's entire upstream proxy
and changing tuning history. The footer explicitly reports readiness for downstream
use after guarded publication; evaluation failures propagate as errors instead of
an indefinitely pending export. Output preparation uses a preparation message,
reserving "Applying bookmark" for configuration restoration.
